mcqs.why: Most covalent compounds consist of non-polar molecules. Water is a polar solvent and dissolves particles that interact with its charges, such as ions and polar molecules. Non-polar molecules are not attracted strongly enough, so they remain undissolved; polar covalent compounds like HCl and sugar are exceptions.

mcqs.q: Which of the following covalent compounds DOES dissolve in water, as an exception?
mcqs.why: Most covalent compounds are insoluble in water, but polar covalent compounds are exceptions: HCl dissolves and ionises in water, and sugar also dissolves. Wax, oils and plastics are non-polar and do not dissolve.

mcqs.q: Metals conduct heat well because:
options: Free electrons gain kinetic energy at the hot end and carry it rapidly to the colder parts
Air trapped in metals carries the heat
Their atoms are not bonded to each other
mcqs.why: Metals contain free (mobile) electrons. When one end is heated, the electrons there gain kinetic energy and move rapidly towards the colder parts, carrying the energy with them; the vibrating ions also pass energy to neighbours. This fast transfer by free electrons makes metals good conductors of heat.

mcqs.q: Nitrogen forms how many well-known oxides?
mcqs.why: Nitrogen forms five well-known oxides: nitrous oxide N2O, nitric oxide NO, nitrogen trioxide N2O3, nitrogen dioxide NO2 (in equilibrium with its dimer N2O4) and nitrogen pentoxide N2O5.

mcqs.q: The formula of nitrogen pentoxide is:
mcqs.why: Nitrogen's five oxides are N2O (nitrous oxide), NO (nitric oxide), N2O3 (nitrogen trioxide), NO2 (nitrogen dioxide) and N2O5 (nitrogen pentoxide) - the pentoxide contains two nitrogen and five oxygen atoms.

mcqs.q: When aqueous NaBr is treated with AgNO3 solution, the product formed as a precipitate is:
mcqs.why: Both salts are soluble and ionic, so a double decomposition (precipitation) reaction occurs: NaBr + AgNO3 -> AgBr + NaNO3. Silver bromide is insoluble and separates as a pale yellow precipitate, while sodium nitrate stays in solution.

mcqs.q: Iodine exists as a solid at room temperature while chlorine is a gas because:
options: Iodine has hydrogen bonding but chlorine does not
I2 molecules are much larger and heavier, so the van der Waals forces between them are much stronger
mcqs.why: The van der Waals forces between molecules increase with molecular size and mass. I2 molecules are much larger and heavier than Cl2 molecules, so the forces between them are strong enough to hold iodine in a solid lattice, while the weak forces between small Cl2 molecules leave chlorine a gas.

mcqs.q: The forces that decide whether a molecular substance is a solid, liquid or gas at room temperature are:
options: The covalent bonds inside its molecules
The intermolecular (van der Waals) forces between its molecules
The nuclear forces in its atoms
mcqs.why: The covalent bonds inside molecules like I2 and Cl2 stay intact in all three states. What changes with state is how strongly the molecules attract one another: strong van der Waals forces (large I2) give a solid, weak forces (small Cl2) give a gas.

lessons.title: Descriptive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 4(i) Explain the formation of an ionic bond and a covalent bond.

An ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of one or more electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom: the metal becomes a positive ion and the non-metal a negative ion, and the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions is the ionic bond, e.g. Na loses its outer electron to Cl forming NaCl. A covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of electrons between two non-metal atoms: the shared pair is attracted by both nuclei and holds the atoms together, e.g. the H-H bond in H2 or the four C-H bonds in CH4. Sharing one, two or three pairs gives single, double or triple covalent bonds.

Q: 4(ii) How do ions arange themselves to form NaCl crystal.

In solid NaCl each Na+ ion is surrounded by six Cl- ions and each Cl- ion by six Na+ ions, in a regular three-dimensional cubic lattice. The ions arrange themselves so that the attraction between opposite charges is maximum and the repulsion between like charges is minimum, giving a stable crystal. There are no separate NaCl molecules; the whole crystal is one giant ionic structure with the ratio of Na+ to Cl- equal to 1:1.

Q: 4(iii) Explain the properties of metals keeping in view the nature of metellic bond.

A metallic bond is the attraction between the positive metal ions and the sea of free electrons around them. This explains the properties of metals: (1) Electrical and thermal conductivity, because the free electrons move and carry charge and energy. (2) Malleability and ductility, because the bond is non-directional and layers of ions can slide without breaking it. (3) High melting points (in most metals), because many ions are held strongly by the electron sea. (4) Metallic lustre, because the free electrons absorb and re-emit light.

Q: 4(iv) Compare the properties of ionic and covalent compounds.

Ionic compounds: formed by transfer of electrons; exist as giant crystal lattices of ions; high melting and boiling points; hard and brittle solids; conduct electricity when molten or in solution but not as solids; generally soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents. Covalent compounds: formed by sharing of electrons; exist as separate molecules; low melting and boiling points; mostly gases, liquids or soft solids; do not conduct electricity (except graphite); generally insoluble in water and soluble in organic solvents.

Q: 4(v) How will you explain the electrical conductivity of graphite crystals?

In graphite each carbon atom is bonded to three others in hexagonal layers, so one electron of every carbon atom is left free. These free electrons are mobile between the layers and can carry charge through the crystal when a potential difference is applied. Hence graphite conducts electricity, unlike diamond in which all four electrons of each carbon are used in bonds and none is free.

Q: 4(vi) Why are metals usually hard and heavy?

Metals are hard because their positive ions are packed closely and held strongly by the sea of electrons, so a large force is needed to disturb the structure. They are heavy (dense) because the atoms of metals are relatively heavy and are packed tightly together in the lattice with very little empty space between them.

mcqs.q: An ionic bond is formed by:
options: Mutual sharing of electrons between two non-metals
Donation of a lone pair by one atom only
Complete transfer of one or more electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom
A sea of electrons around positive ions
mcqs.why: In ionic bonding a metal atom transfers one or more electrons completely to a non-metal atom: the metal becomes a positive ion and the non-metal a negative ion, and the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions is the ionic bond, e.g. NaCl.

mcqs.q: A covalent bond is formed by:
options: Complete transfer of electrons to a metal
Attraction between positive ions and an electron sea
Mutual sharing of electrons between two non-metal atoms
mcqs.why: In covalent bonding two non-metal atoms mutually share electrons; the shared pair is attracted by both nuclei and holds the atoms together, e.g. H-H in H2 and the four C-H bonds in CH4. Sharing one, two or three pairs gives single, double or triple bonds.

mcqs.q: In a crystal of NaCl, each Na+ ion is surrounded by:
mcqs.why: In solid NaCl each Na+ ion is surrounded by six Cl- ions and each Cl- ion by six Na+ ions in a regular three-dimensional cubic lattice, arranged so that attraction between opposite charges is maximum and repulsion between like charges is minimum.

mcqs.q: Solid NaCl does not consist of separate NaCl molecules because:
options: NaCl is a gas at room temperature
The whole crystal is one giant ionic structure with Na+ and Cl- in the ratio 1:1
The ions share electrons in pairs
Sodium and chlorine do not react
mcqs.why: There are no separate NaCl molecules in the solid. Each ion is held by all its oppositely charged neighbours, so the whole crystal is one giant ionic structure; the formula NaCl only gives the 1:1 ratio of the ions.

mcqs.q: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in solution, but not as solids, because:
options: Ions carry no charge in the solid state
Their ions are locked in the solid lattice but become free to move when molten or dissolved
mcqs.why: In a solid ionic compound the ions are locked in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move to carry charge. On melting or dissolving, the lattice breaks down and the ions move freely, so the compound conducts electricity.

mcqs.q: Compared with ionic compounds, covalent compounds generally have:
options: Free ions in the solid state
Low melting and boiling points and exist as separate molecules
mcqs.why: Covalent compounds are formed by sharing electrons and exist as separate molecules held by weak intermolecular forces, so they have low melting and boiling points and are mostly gases, liquids or soft solids. Ionic compounds form giant lattices with high melting and boiling points.

mcqs.q: Graphite conducts electricity because:
options: One electron of each carbon atom is left free and mobile between the layers
All its electrons are used in bonds
It dissolves in water to give ions
mcqs.why: In graphite each carbon atom is bonded to three others in hexagonal layers, leaving one electron of every atom free. These mobile electrons carry charge through the crystal, so graphite conducts electricity - unlike diamond, where all four electrons of each carbon are used in bonds.

mcqs.q: Diamond does not conduct electricity because:
options: All four electrons of each carbon atom are used in covalent bonds, so none is free
Its atoms are too far apart
mcqs.why: In diamond every carbon atom uses all four of its outer electrons in covalent bonds with four neighbours. With no free or mobile electrons, diamond cannot carry charge and is an electrical insulator - the opposite of graphite.

mcqs.q: Metals are usually heavy (dense) because:
options: Their relatively heavy atoms are packed tightly together with very little empty space
mcqs.why: Metals are hard and heavy: their positive ions are packed closely and held strongly by the sea of electrons, and the atoms themselves are relatively heavy and packed tightly in the lattice with very little empty space, giving high density.

mcqs.q: The metallic lustre (shine) of metals is due to:
options: A layer of polish on the surface
Free electrons absorbing and re-emitting light
mcqs.why: The sea of free electrons in a metal absorbs light falling on the surface and re-emits it, which gives metals their characteristic shiny appearance - metallic lustre.

lessons.title: Investigative Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 5(i) The formula of AlCl3 in vapour phase is Al2Cl6 which means it exists as a dimer. Explain the bonding between its two molecules?

An AlCl3 molecule is electron-deficient: the aluminium atom has only six electrons in its outer shell. In the vapour, two AlCl3 molecules join together so that a chlorine atom of each molecule donates a lone pair into the empty orbital of the aluminium of the other molecule, forming two coordinate covalent (dative) bonds across the pair. The dimer Al2Cl6 thus has two bridging chlorine atoms, each joined to one aluminium by a covalent bond and to the other by a coordinate bond, and each aluminium completes its octet.

Q: 5(ii) Explain the structure of sand (SiO2).

Sand, SiO2, has a giant covalent (network) structure like that of diamond. Each silicon atom is bonded tetrahedrally to four oxygen atoms, and each oxygen atom is shared between two silicon atoms, so the ratio Si:O is 1:2. The whole structure is one continuous three-dimensional network of strong Si-O covalent bonds, which is why sand has a very high melting point, is hard and does not conduct electricity.

mcqs.q: In the vapour phase, aluminium chloride exists as a dimer with the formula:
mcqs.why: Although the simple formula of aluminium chloride is AlCl3, in the vapour phase two molecules join together as a dimer, Al2Cl6, held together by coordinate bonds through bridging chlorine atoms.

mcqs.q: An AlCl3 molecule is electron-deficient because the aluminium atom has only:
options: Six electrons in its outer shell
Eight electrons in its outer shell
Two electrons in its outer shell
Four electrons in its outer shell
mcqs.why: In AlCl3 the aluminium atom shares three pairs of electrons, giving it only six electrons in its outer shell - two short of an octet. This electron deficiency is why AlCl3 accepts a lone pair and forms the dimer Al2Cl6.

mcqs.q: In the Al2Cl6 dimer, each bridging chlorine atom is joined to the two aluminium atoms by:
options: One covalent bond and one coordinate bond
One hydrogen bond and one covalent bond
mcqs.why: Each bridging chlorine is joined to one aluminium by an ordinary covalent bond and to the other aluminium by a coordinate bond, in which the chlorine donates a lone pair into the empty orbital of the aluminium. There are two such bridging chlorines in Al2Cl6.

mcqs.q: The coordinate bonds in Al2Cl6 are formed when a chlorine atom:
options: Transfers an electron completely to aluminium
Donates a lone pair into the empty orbital of an aluminium atom of the other molecule
mcqs.why: A chlorine atom of one AlCl3 molecule donates a lone pair into the empty orbital of the aluminium atom of the other molecule. Two such dative (coordinate) bonds form across the pair of molecules, producing the dimer.

mcqs.q: After dimerisation in Al2Cl6, each aluminium atom:
options: Completes its octet of outer electrons
mcqs.why: By accepting a lone pair from a bridging chlorine, each aluminium in Al2Cl6 gains two more electrons and completes its octet (eight outer electrons), which is the driving force for dimer formation.

mcqs.q: Sand (SiO2) has a structure best described as:
options: A giant covalent network like that of diamond
An ionic lattice of Si4+ and O2- ions
Layers that slide over one another
mcqs.why: Sand has a giant covalent (network) structure like diamond: each silicon atom is bonded tetrahedrally to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen is shared between two silicon atoms, forming one continuous three-dimensional network of strong Si-O bonds.

mcqs.q: In the SiO2 network, each silicon atom is bonded to:
options: Two oxygen atoms in a line
mcqs.why: Each silicon atom in sand is bonded tetrahedrally to four oxygen atoms, and each oxygen atom is shared between two silicon atoms - which is why the overall ratio of Si to O is 1:2.

mcqs.q: Each oxygen atom in SiO2 is shared between:
mcqs.why: Every oxygen atom in the SiO2 network bridges two silicon atoms. Counting the sharing: each Si has 4 oxygens, each shared by 2 silicons, giving 4 x 1/2 = 2 oxygens per silicon - the ratio Si:O = 1:2.

mcqs.q: Sand has a very high melting point because:
options: Its whole structure is one continuous network of strong Si-O covalent bonds that must be broken
mcqs.why: To melt sand, the strong Si-O covalent bonds running through the entire three-dimensional network must be broken, which needs a great deal of energy. Hence sand has a very high melting point and is hard.

mcqs.q: Sand does not conduct electricity because it has:
options: No free electrons and no mobile ions
mcqs.why: In SiO2 all electrons are locked in covalent bonds and there are no ions at all, so there are no charge carriers. Sand therefore does not conduct electricity, unlike graphite (free electrons) or molten ionic compounds (mobile ions).

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 1(i) How many atoms are present in one gram of H2O?

(a) 1002 x 10^23 atoms (b) 6.022 x 10^23 atoms (c) 0.334 x 10^23 atoms (d) 2.004 x 10^23 atoms
Correct answer: 1002 x 10^23 atoms

Q: Note: How is the answer to 1(i) obtained?

Working: moles of H2O in 1 g = 1 / 18 = 0.0556 mol. Molecules = 0.0556 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 0.334 x 10^23. Each molecule has 3 atoms, so atoms = 3 x 0.334 x 10^23 = 1.002 x 10^23 atoms. Option (a) is the intended answer; in the book it is printed as '1002 x 10^23', which appears to be a misprint for 1.002 x 10^23.

Q: 1(ii) Which is the correct formula of calcium phosphide?

(a) CaP (b) CaP2 (c) Ca2P3 (d) Ca3P2
Correct answer: Ca3P2

Q: 1(iii) How many atomic mass units (amu) are there in one gram?

(a) 1 amu (b) 10^23 amu (c) 6.022 x 10^23 amu (d) 6.022 x 10^22 amu
Correct answer: 6.022 x 10^23 amu

Q: 1(iv) Structural formula of 2-hexene is CH3 - CH = CH - (CH2)2 - CH3. What will be its empirical formula?

(a) C2H2 (b) CH (c) C6H12 (d) CH2
Correct answer: CH2

Q: 1(v) How many moles are there in 25 g of H2SO4?

(a) 0.765 moles (b) 0.51 moles (c) 0.255 moles (d) 0.4 moles
Correct answer: 0.255 moles

Q: 1(vi) A necklace has 6g of diamonds in it. What are the number of carbon atoms in it?

(a) 6.02 x 10^23 (b) 12.04 x 10^23 (c) 1.003 x 10^23 (d) 3.01 x 10^23
Correct answer: 3.01 x 10^23

Q: 1(vii) What is the mass of Al in 204g of aluminium oxide, Al2O3.

(a) 26g (b) 27g (c) 54g (d) 108g
Correct answer: 108g

Q: 1(viii) Which one of the following compounds will have the highest percentage of the mass of nitrogen?

(a) CO(NH2)2 (b) N2H4 (c) NH3 (d) NH2OH
Correct answer: N2H4

Q: 1(ix) When one mole of each of the following compounds is reacted with oxygen, which will produce the maximum amount of CO2?

(a) Carbon (b) Diamond (c) Ethane (C2H6) (d) Methane (CH4)
Correct answer: Ethane (C2H6)

Q: 1(x) What mass of 95% CaCO3 will be required to neutralize 50 cm3 of 0.5M HCl solution?

(a) 9.5g (b) 1.25g (c) 1.32g (d) 1.45g
Correct answer: 1.32g

mcqs.q: 1(i) How many atoms are present in one gram of H2O?
mcqs.why: Working: moles of H2O in 1 g = 1 / 18 = 0.0556 mol. Molecules = 0.0556 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 0.334 x 10^23. Each H2O molecule contains 3 atoms, so atoms = 3 x 0.334 x 10^23 = 1.002 x 10^23 atoms. Note: the book prints option (a) as '1002 x 10^23', which is a misprint for 1.002 x 10^23; (a) is the intended answer, as the Note after this question in the book explains.

mcqs.q: 1(ii) Which is the correct formula of calcium phosphide?
mcqs.why: Calcium forms Ca2+ ions and phosphorus forms phosphide ions, P3-. To balance the charges, 3 x (+2) + 2 x (-3) = 0, so three Ca2+ combine with two P3- and the formula is Ca3P2.

mcqs.q: 1(iii) How many atomic mass units (amu) are there in one gram?
mcqs.why: By definition, one atomic mass unit is 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, and Avogadro's number (6.022 x 10^23) of atomic mass units make exactly one gram. So one gram contains 6.022 x 10^23 amu.

mcqs.q: 1(iv) Structural formula of 2-hexene is CH3 - CH = CH - (CH2)2 - CH3. What will be its empirical formula?
mcqs.why: 2-Hexene has 6 carbon and 12 hydrogen atoms, C6H12. The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms: 6:12 reduces to 1:2, giving CH2.

mcqs.q: 1(v) How many moles are there in 25 g of H2SO4?
mcqs.why: Working: molar mass of H2SO4 = 2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 98 g/mol. Moles = mass / molar mass = 25 / 98 = 0.255 mol.

mcqs.q: 1(vi) A necklace has 6g of diamonds in it. What are the number of carbon atoms in it?
mcqs.why: Working: diamond is carbon (atomic mass 12). Moles of C = 6 / 12 = 0.5 mol. Number of atoms = 0.5 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 3.01 x 10^23 atoms.

mcqs.q: 1(vii) What is the mass of Al in 204g of aluminium oxide, Al2O3.
mcqs.why: Working: molar mass of Al2O3 = 2(27) + 3(16) = 102 g/mol, of which aluminium contributes 2 x 27 = 54 g. In 204 g (two formula masses) the mass of Al = 2 x 54 = 108 g.

mcqs.q: 1(viii) Which one of the following compounds will have the highest percentage of the mass of nitrogen?
mcqs.why: Working (percentage of N): urea CO(NH2)2 = 28/60 x 100 = 46.7%; N2H4 = 28/32 x 100 = 87.5%; NH3 = 14/17 x 100 = 82.4%; NH2OH = 14/33 x 100 = 42.4%. N2H4 has the highest percentage of nitrogen.

mcqs.q: 1(ix) When one mole of each of the following compounds is reacted with oxygen, which will produce the maximum amount of CO2?
mcqs.why: Each mole of a compound gives as many moles of CO2 as the carbon atoms in its formula. Carbon, diamond and methane CH4 each give 1 mole of CO2 per mole, but one mole of ethane C2H6 contains 2 moles of carbon atoms and produces 2 moles of CO2 - the maximum.

mcqs.q: 1(x) What mass of 95% CaCO3 will be required to neutralize 50 cm3 of 0.5M HCl solution?
mcqs.why: Working: moles of HCl = (50/1000) x 0.5 = 0.025 mol. CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O, so moles of CaCO3 = 0.025/2 = 0.0125 mol; mass of pure CaCO3 = 0.0125 x 100 = 1.25 g. The sample is only 95% pure, so mass required = 1.25 / 0.95 = 1.32 g.

lessons.title: Questions for Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 2(i) Write down the chemical formula of barium nitride.

Barium is Ba2+ and nitride is N3-. To balance the charges, three Ba2+ ions (total +6) combine with two N3- ions (total -6). Formula: Ba3N2.

Q: 2(ii) Find out the molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH2O and its molar mass is 180.

Step 1 - Empirical formula mass of CH2O = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. Step 2 - Formula: n = molar mass / empirical formula mass = 180 / 30 = 6. Step 3 - Molecular formula = (CH2O) x 6 = C6H12O6.

Q: 2(iii) How many molecules are present in 1.5 g H2O?

Step 1 - Moles of H2O = mass / molar mass = 1.5 / 18 = 0.0833 mol. Step 2 - Formula: number of molecules = moles x Avogadro's number. Step 3 - Substitute: = 0.0833 x 6.022 x 10^23. Step 4 - Final answer: 5.02 x 10^22 molecules.

Q: 2(iv) What is the difference between a mole and Avogadro's number?

Avogadro's number is a pure number, 6.022 x 10^23, the number of particles in one mole of a substance. A mole is the amount of substance that contains Avogadro's number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions); it is a quantity/unit of amount, whereas Avogadro's number is the count per mole.

Q: 2(v) Write down the chemical equation of the following reaction. Copper + Sulphuric acid -> Copper sulphate + Sulphur dioxide + Water

Cu + 2H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O. (Hot concentrated sulphuric acid oxidises copper; the equation is balanced: Cu 1, H 4, S 2, O 8 on both sides.)

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of barium nitride is:
mcqs.why: Barium forms Ba2+ ions and nitrogen forms nitride ions, N3-. Three Ba2+ ions give a total charge of +6 and two N3- ions give -6, balancing each other, so the formula is Ba3N2.

mcqs.q: A compound has empirical formula CH2O and molar mass 180. Its molecular formula is:
mcqs.why: Working: empirical formula mass of CH2O = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. n = molar mass / empirical formula mass = 180 / 30 = 6. Molecular formula = (CH2O) x 6 = C6H12O6 (glucose).

mcqs.q: The empirical formula mass of CH2O is:
mcqs.why: Working: empirical formula mass = mass of C + 2 x mass of H + mass of O = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30. This is divided into the molar mass to find how many empirical units are in the molecule.

mcqs.q: How many molecules are present in 1.5 g of H2O?
mcqs.why: Working: moles of H2O = 1.5 / 18 = 0.0833 mol. Number of molecules = moles x Avogadro's number = 0.0833 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 5.02 x 10^22 molecules.

mcqs.q: The difference between a mole and Avogadro's number is that:
options: A mole is a pure number and Avogadro's number is a unit
A mole is an amount of substance, while Avogadro's number is the count of particles (6.022 x 10^23) in one mole
They are two names for exactly the same thing
Avogadro's number applies only to gases
mcqs.why: Avogadro's number is a pure number, 6.022 x 10^23 - the number of particles in one mole. A mole is the amount of substance that contains this number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions); it is a quantity of amount, whereas Avogadro's number is the count per mole.

mcqs.q: The balanced equation for copper reacting with (hot concentrated) sulphuric acid is:
mcqs.why: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid oxidises copper: Cu + 2H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O. The equation is balanced: Cu 1, H 4, S 2 and O 8 atoms on both sides. (With dilute acid, copper does not give hydrogen like an ordinary metal-acid reaction.)

mcqs.q: In the equation Cu + 2H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O, the coefficient of H2SO4 is:
mcqs.why: Two molecules of sulphuric acid are needed: one provides the sulphate for CuSO4 and the other is reduced to SO2. Counting atoms confirms the balance: H = 4, S = 2, O = 8 on each side of the equation.

mcqs.q: The number of empirical-formula units (n) in a molecule is found by:
options: n = molar mass / empirical formula mass
n = empirical formula mass / molar mass
n = molar mass x empirical formula mass
n = molar mass - empirical formula mass
mcqs.why: The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula. That multiple is n = molar mass / empirical formula mass, e.g. for CH2O with molar mass 180: n = 180 / 30 = 6.

mcqs.q: The number of moles in 1.5 g of water is:
mcqs.why: Working: moles = mass / molar mass = 1.5 / 18 = 0.0833 mol. Multiplying by Avogadro's number then gives the number of molecules, 5.02 x 10^22.

mcqs.q: The charge on the nitride ion, used in writing formulae such as Ba3N2, is:
mcqs.why: Nitrogen gains three electrons to complete its octet, forming the nitride ion N3-. In barium nitride, two N3- ions (total -6) balance three Ba2+ ions (total +6), giving Ba3N2.

lessons.title: Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 3(i) Different compounds will never have the same moleculer formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain

The molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule, so it identifies the compound exactly; two different compounds cannot have the same molecular formula. The empirical formula shows only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, and different compounds with the same ratio share it: for example glucose C6H12O6, acetic acid C2H4O2 and formaldehyde CH2O all have the empirical formula CH2O although they are different compounds.

Q: 3(ii) Write down the chemical formulas of the following compounds. Calcium phosphate, Aluminium nitride, Sodium acetate, Ammonium carbonate and Bismuth sulphate.

Calcium phosphate: Ca3(PO4)2. Aluminium nitride: AlN. Sodium acetate: CH3COONa. Ammonium carbonate: (NH4)2CO3. Bismuth sulphate: Bi2(SO4)3.

Q: 3(iii) Why does Avogadro's number have an immense importance in chemistry?

Atoms and molecules are far too small to be counted or weighed one by one. Avogadro's number connects the invisible particle scale with the weighable laboratory scale: knowing that one mole always contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles, a chemist can find the number of particles in any weighed sample and can calculate the masses of reactants and products in any reaction. It is the bridge between the atomic world and everyday quantities.

Q: 3(iv) When 8.657g of a compound were converted into elements, it gave 5.217g of carbon, 0.962g of hydrogen and 2.478g of oxygen. Calculate the percentage of each element present in this compound.

Given data: mass of compound = 8.657 g; carbon = 5.217 g; hydrogen = 0.962 g; oxygen = 2.478 g. Step 1 - Formula: percentage of an element = (mass of element / mass of compound) x 100. Step 2 - Carbon: = (5.217 / 8.657) x 100 = 60.26%. Step 3 - Hydrogen: = (0.962 / 8.657) x 100 = 11.11%. Step 4 - Oxygen: = (2.478 / 8.657) x 100 = 28.62%. Step 5 - Check: 60.26 + 11.11 + 28.62 = 99.99%, approximately 100%. Final answer: C = 60.26%, H = 11.11%, O = 28.62%.

Q: 3(v) How can you calculate the masses of the products formed in a reversible reaction?

A reversible reaction does not go to completion; it reaches equilibrium with reactants and products present together. The mass of products actually obtained depends on the position of equilibrium, so it is found from the equilibrium amounts: either from the given equilibrium data (moles or masses at equilibrium) using the mole ratio of the balanced equation, or by using the percentage yield: actual mass = percentage yield x theoretical mass calculated for a complete reaction. Simply applying the equation as if the reaction were complete would overstate the products.

mcqs.q: Different compounds can have the same empirical formula because the empirical formula shows:
options: The exact structure of the molecule
The actual number of atoms in one molecule
Only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, not the actual number of atoms
The mass of one mole of the compound
mcqs.why: The molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element and identifies a compound exactly, so two different compounds never share it. The empirical formula shows only the simplest ratio: glucose C6H12O6, acetic acid C2H4O2 and formaldehyde CH2O are different compounds but all have the empirical formula CH2O.

mcqs.q: Glucose (C6H12O6), acetic acid (C2H4O2) and formaldehyde (CH2O) all share the empirical formula:
mcqs.why: In each compound the ratio C:H:O reduces to 1:2:1 - for glucose 6:12:6, for acetic acid 2:4:2, and formaldehyde is already 1:2:1. So all three have the empirical formula CH2O although they are different compounds.

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of calcium phosphate is:
mcqs.why: Calcium is Ca2+ and phosphate is PO4 3-. To balance charges, 3 x (+2) + 2 x (-3) = 0, so three calcium ions combine with two phosphate ions: Ca3(PO4)2. The brackets show that the subscript 2 applies to the whole phosphate group.

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of aluminium nitride is:
mcqs.why: Aluminium forms Al3+ and nitrogen forms N3-. Equal and opposite charges balance in a 1:1 ratio, so the formula is simply AlN.

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of sodium acetate is:
mcqs.why: Sodium acetate is the sodium salt of acetic acid, CH3COOH; replacing the acidic hydrogen by sodium gives CH3COONa, containing the acetate group CH3COO- with Na+.

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of ammonium carbonate is:
mcqs.why: Ammonium is NH4+ and carbonate is CO3 2-. Two ammonium ions (+1 each) balance one carbonate ion (-2), so the formula is (NH4)2CO3; the brackets show both hydrogens and nitrogens belong to two ammonium groups.

mcqs.q: The chemical formula of bismuth sulphate is:
mcqs.why: Bismuth forms Bi3+ and sulphate is SO4 2-. Balancing charges: 2 x (+3) + 3 x (-2) = 0, so two bismuth ions combine with three sulphate groups: Bi2(SO4)3.

mcqs.q: Avogadro's number is immensely important in chemistry because it:
options: Tells us the colour of every compound
Connects the invisible particle scale with the weighable laboratory scale
Replaces the need for balanced equations
mcqs.why: Atoms and molecules are far too small to count or weigh one by one. Since one mole always contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles, Avogadro's number lets a chemist find the number of particles in any weighed sample and calculate the masses of reactants and products - it is the bridge between the atomic world and everyday quantities.

mcqs.q: When 8.657 g of a compound gave 5.217 g of carbon, 0.962 g of hydrogen and 2.478 g of oxygen, the percentage of carbon in the compound is:
mcqs.why: Working: percentage of an element = (mass of element / mass of compound) x 100. Carbon = (5.217 / 8.657) x 100 = 60.26%. (Similarly H = 11.11% and O = 28.62%; the three add up to 99.99%, about 100%.)

mcqs.q: The masses of products formed in a reversible reaction are calculated from:
options: The balanced equation alone, assuming the reaction goes to completion
The equilibrium amounts, or from the percentage yield of the theoretical mass
mcqs.why: A reversible reaction does not go to completion; it reaches equilibrium with reactants and products together. Product masses therefore come from the equilibrium amounts using the mole ratio, or from actual mass = percentage yield x theoretical mass. Applying the equation as if the reaction were complete would overstate the products.

lessons.title: Descriptive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 4(i) Which conditions must be fulfilled before writing a chemical equation for a reaction?

Before writing a chemical equation we must know: (1) the correct names and formulae of all the reactants and products taking part; (2) the physical states of the substances; (3) the conditions of the reaction (heat, pressure, catalyst, etc.); and the equation written must be balanced so that it obeys the law of conservation of mass, with equal numbers of atoms of each element on both sides.

Q: 4(ii) Explain the concepts of Avogadro's number and mole.

Avogadro's number is the number of particles (atoms, molecules or ions) present in one mole of a substance; its value is 6.022 x 10^23. A mole is the amount of a substance that contains Avogadro's number of particles; the mass of one mole, expressed in grams, is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass of the substance and is called its molar mass. For example, one mole of carbon contains 6.022 x 10^23 atoms and has a mass of 12 g; one mole of water contains 6.022 x 10^23 molecules and has a mass of 18 g.

Q: 4(iii) How many grams of CO2 will be produced when we react 10 g of CH4 with excess of O2 according to the following equation? CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(g)

Given data: mass of CH4 = 10 g; equation: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. Step 1 - Moles of CH4 = mass / molar mass = 10 / 16 = 0.625 mol. Step 2 - Mole ratio from the equation: 1 mole of CH4 produces 1 mole of CO2, so moles of CO2 = 0.625 mol. Step 3 - Formula: mass = moles x molar mass. Step 4 - Substitute: mass of CO2 = 0.625 x 44 = 27.5 g. Final answer: 27.5 g of CO2 will be produced.

Q: 4(iv) How many moles of coal are needed to produce 10 moles of CO according to the following equation? 3C(s) + O2(g) + H2O(l) -> H2(g) + 3CO(g)

Given data: equation: 3C + O2 + H2O -> H2 + 3CO; CO required = 10 moles. Step 1 - Mole ratio from the equation: 3 moles of carbon (coal) produce 3 moles of CO, i.e. the ratio C : CO is 1 : 1. Step 2 - Therefore moles of coal needed = 10 x (3/3) = 10 moles. Final answer: 10 moles of coal are needed to produce 10 moles of CO.

Q: 4(v) How much SO2 is needed in grams to produce 10 moles of sulphur? 2H2S(g) + SO2(g) -> 2H2O(l) + 3S(s)

Given data: equation: 2H2S + SO2 -> 2H2O + 3S; sulphur required = 10 moles. Step 1 - Mole ratio: 1 mole of SO2 produces 3 moles of S. Step 2 - Moles of SO2 needed = 10 / 3 = 3.33 mol. Step 3 - Formula: mass = moles x molar mass; molar mass of SO2 = 32 + 32 = 64 g/mol. Step 4 - Substitute: mass of SO2 = 3.33 x 64 = 213.3 g. Final answer: 213.3 g of SO2 is needed.

Q: 4(vi) How much ammonia is needed in grams to produce 1 kg of urea fertilizer? 2NH3(aq) + CO2(aq) -> CO(NH2)2(aq) + H2O(l)

Given data: equation: 2NH3 + CO2 -> CO(NH2)2 + H2O; urea required = 1 kg = 1000 g. Step 1 - Molar mass of urea = 12 + 16 + 2 x (14 + 2) = 60 g/mol; moles of urea = 1000 / 60 = 16.67 mol. Step 2 - Mole ratio: 2 moles of NH3 produce 1 mole of urea, so moles of NH3 = 2 x 16.67 = 33.33 mol. Step 3 - Formula: mass = moles x molar mass; molar mass of NH3 = 17 g/mol. Step 4 - Substitute: mass of NH3 = 33.33 x 17 = 566.7 g. Final answer: 566.7 g of ammonia is needed.

Q: 4(vii) Calculate the number of atoms in the following. (a) 3g of H2 (b) 3.4 moles of N2 (c) 10g of C6H12O6.

(a) 3 g of H2: Step 1 - Moles of H2 = 3 / 2 = 1.5 mol. Step 2 - Molecules = 1.5 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 9.03 x 10^23. Step 3 - Each molecule has 2 atoms, so atoms = 2 x 9.03 x 10^23 = 1.81 x 10^24 atoms. (b) 3.4 moles of N2: Step 1 - Molecules = 3.4 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 2.05 x 10^24. Step 2 - Atoms = 2 x 2.05 x 10^24 = 4.09 x 10^24 atoms. (c) 10 g of C6H12O6: Step 1 - Molar mass = 6 x 12 + 12 x 1 + 6 x 16 = 180 g/mol; moles = 10 / 180 = 0.0556 mol. Step 2 - Molecules = 0.0556 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 3.35 x 10^22. Step 3 - Each molecule has 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms, so atoms = 24 x 3.35 x 10^22 = 8.03 x 10^23 atoms.

mcqs.q: Before writing a chemical equation for a reaction, we must know:
options: Only the names of the products
The colour of each substance only
The correct formulae of all reactants and products, their physical states and the reaction conditions
mcqs.why: A correct equation needs: (1) the correct names and formulae of all reactants and products; (2) the physical states of the substances; (3) the conditions (heat, pressure, catalyst). The equation must then be balanced to obey the law of conservation of mass.

mcqs.q: A balanced chemical equation obeys the:
options: Law of conservation of mass, with equal numbers of atoms of each element on both sides
Law of conservation of energy only
Law of definite proportions of gases
Rule that products are always heavier
mcqs.why: Balancing makes the number of atoms of each element equal on the two sides of the equation, so the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products - the law of conservation of mass.

mcqs.q: The molar mass of a substance is:
options: The mass of one atom in grams
The mass of one mole of it in grams, numerically equal to its atomic or molecular mass
The number of particles in one mole
mcqs.why: One mole of a substance contains Avogadro's number (6.022 x 10^23) of particles. Its mass in grams - the molar mass - is numerically equal to its atomic or molecular mass: one mole of carbon is 12 g and one mole of water is 18 g.

mcqs.q: How many grams of CO2 are produced when 10 g of CH4 react with excess O2 (CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O)?
mcqs.why: Working: moles of CH4 = 10 / 16 = 0.625 mol. From the equation, 1 mole of CH4 produces 1 mole of CO2, so moles of CO2 = 0.625 mol. Mass of CO2 = 0.625 x 44 = 27.5 g.

mcqs.q: According to 3C + O2 + H2O -> H2 + 3CO, the moles of coal (carbon) needed to produce 10 moles of CO are:
mcqs.why: Working: from the equation, 3 moles of carbon produce 3 moles of CO, so the ratio C:CO is 1:1. Moles of coal needed = 10 x (3/3) = 10 moles.

mcqs.q: How much SO2 (in grams) is needed to produce 10 moles of sulphur (2H2S + SO2 -> 2H2O + 3S)?
mcqs.why: Working: 1 mole of SO2 produces 3 moles of S, so moles of SO2 = 10 / 3 = 3.33 mol. Molar mass of SO2 = 32 + 2(16) = 64 g/mol. Mass = 3.33 x 64 = 213.3 g.

mcqs.q: How much ammonia is needed to produce 1 kg of urea (2NH3 + CO2 -> CO(NH2)2 + H2O)?
mcqs.why: Working: molar mass of urea = 12 + 16 + 2(14 + 2) = 60 g/mol; moles of urea = 1000 / 60 = 16.67 mol. From the equation 2 moles of NH3 give 1 mole of urea, so moles of NH3 = 2 x 16.67 = 33.33 mol. Mass of NH3 = 33.33 x 17 = 566.7 g.

mcqs.q: The number of atoms in 3 g of H2 is:
mcqs.why: Working: moles of H2 = 3 / 2 = 1.5 mol. Molecules = 1.5 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 9.03 x 10^23. Each H2 molecule has 2 atoms, so atoms = 2 x 9.03 x 10^23 = 1.81 x 10^24 atoms. (9.03 x 10^23 is the number of molecules - the trap in this question.)

mcqs.q: The number of atoms in 10 g of glucose, C6H12O6, is:
mcqs.why: Working: molar mass of C6H12O6 = 6(12) + 12(1) + 6(16) = 180 g/mol; moles = 10 / 180 = 0.0556 mol. Molecules = 0.0556 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 3.35 x 10^22. Each molecule has 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms, so atoms = 24 x 3.35 x 10^22 = 8.03 x 10^23 atoms.

mcqs.q: The number of atoms in 3.4 moles of N2 is:
mcqs.why: Working: molecules of N2 = 3.4 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 2.05 x 10^24. Each N2 molecule contains 2 atoms, so atoms = 2 x 2.05 x 10^24 = 4.09 x 10^24 atoms.

lessons.title: Investigative Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 5(i) It is generally believed that drinking eight glasses of water every day is required to keep oneself hydrated especially in the summer. If a glass occupies 400 cm3 of water on the average, how many moles of water are needed for a single adult?

Step 1 - Volume of water = 8 glasses x 400 cm3 = 3200 cm3. Step 2 - Mass of water: density of water is 1 g/cm3, so mass = 3200 g. Step 3 - Formula: moles = mass / molar mass. Step 4 - Substitute: moles = 3200 / 18 = 177.8. Final answer: about 178 moles of water are needed for a single adult per day.

Q: 5(ii) The chemical formula for sand is SiO2 but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H2O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?

Sand (SiO2) has a giant covalent network structure (see Chapter 3): each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen atom is shared between two silicon atoms. Counting the atoms in the network, for every one silicon atom there are 4 x 1/2 = 2 oxygen atoms, so the simplest ratio of atoms in the structure is Si : O = 1 : 2. The formula SiO2 is therefore the ratio (empirical) formula of the network, not the formula of a discrete molecule.

mcqs.q: Drinking eight glasses of water a day, each of 400 cm3, a single adult needs about how many moles of water?
mcqs.why: Working: volume = 8 x 400 = 3200 cm3. Density of water is 1 g/cm3, so mass = 3200 g. Moles = mass / molar mass = 3200 / 18 = 177.8, i.e. about 178 moles of water per day.

mcqs.q: The total volume of eight glasses of water at 400 cm3 per glass is:
mcqs.why: Working: 8 glasses x 400 cm3 per glass = 3200 cm3 of water. With density 1 g/cm3 this is 3200 g, which is 3200 / 18 = about 178 moles.

mcqs.q: The mass of 3200 cm3 of water (density 1 g/cm3) is:
mcqs.why: Working: mass = volume x density = 3200 cm3 x 1 g/cm3 = 3200 g. This mass divided by the molar mass of water (18 g/mol) gives about 178 moles.

mcqs.q: The formula SiO2 of sand is best described as:
options: The formula of a single SiO2 molecule
An ionic formula unit of Si4+ and O2-
A molecular formula like that of H2O
The ratio (empirical) formula of a giant network, not the formula of a discrete molecule
mcqs.why: Sand has a giant covalent network: each silicon is bonded to four oxygens and each oxygen is shared between two silicons, so the simplest atom ratio is Si:O = 1:2. SiO2 states this ratio for the network; there are no discrete SiO2 molecules as there are H2O molecules.

mcqs.q: In the SiO2 network, the number of oxygen atoms counted per silicon atom is:
options: 4, because silicon bonds to four oxygens
mcqs.why: Working: each silicon is bonded to 4 oxygen atoms, but each oxygen is shared between 2 silicon atoms, so the oxygens belonging to one silicon = 4 x 1/2 = 2. Hence the ratio Si:O = 1:2 and the formula is SiO2.

mcqs.q: Sand does not exist as discrete molecules because it has:
mcqs.why: In sand the Si-O bonds run continuously through the whole structure in a giant covalent network (Chapter 3). There are no separate SiO2 molecules; the formula only expresses the 1:2 ratio of atoms in the network.

mcqs.q: The number of molecules in about 178 moles of water is approximately:
mcqs.why: Working: number of molecules = moles x Avogadro's number = 177.8 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 1.07 x 10^26 molecules - the huge number of particles in just eight glasses of water.

mcqs.q: If each glass held 200 cm3 instead of 400 cm3, eight glasses would contain about:
mcqs.why: Working: volume = 8 x 200 = 1600 cm3, so mass = 1600 g. Moles = 1600 / 18 = 88.9, about 89 moles - exactly half of the 178 moles for 400 cm3 glasses, as expected.

mcqs.q: The mole calculations for drinking water use the molar mass of water, which is:
mcqs.why: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. This is the divisor used in moles = mass / molar mass, e.g. 3200 / 18 = 177.8 mol for eight 400 cm3 glasses.

mcqs.q: Formulas of giant structures such as SiO2 are determined by:
options: Isolating single molecules and weighing them
Counting the ratio of atoms in the repeating network structure
Measuring the boiling point of the solid
mcqs.why: Because a giant network has no discrete molecules, its formula is found by counting atoms in the structure: each Si is bonded to 4 O atoms, each O shared by 2 Si atoms, giving the simplest ratio Si:O = 1:2, written SiO2.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 1(i) The following reaction is an exothermic reaction. H2 + Cl2 --(Sunlight)--> 2HCl. From where does the energy come to break the bonds of H2 and Cl2?

(a) By collisions between the molecules (b) From sunlight (c) From the surrounding (d) By collisions of the molecules with the walls of the container
Correct answer: From sunlight

Q: 1(ii) Which of the following reactions has the least value of activation energy?

(a) H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> H2O(g) (b) C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g) (c) NaCl(aq) + AgNO3(aq) -> AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq) (d) H2(g) + I2(s) -> 2HI(g)
Correct answer: NaCl(aq) + AgNO3(aq) -> AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq)

Q: 1(iii) Formation of which hydrogen halide from the elements is an endothermic reaction?

(a) HCl (b) HF (c) HBr (d) HI
Correct answer: HI

Q: 1(iv) What are the products of anaerobic respiration?

(a) ATP + CO2 + H2O (b) CO2 + H2O (c) ATP + Ethanol + H2O (d) Ethanol + H2O
Correct answer: ATP + Ethanol + H2O

Q: 1(v) Which reaction do you expect to be a reversible reaction? (Energy profiles (a)-(d) are shown in the book.)

(a) profile (a): products C + D far below reactants A + B (strongly exothermic) (b) profile (b): products C + D at almost the same energy as reactants A + B (c) profile (c): products C + D moderately above reactants A + B (d) profile (d): products C + D far above reactants A + B (strongly endothermic)
Correct answer: profile (b): products C + D at almost the same energy as reactants A + B

Q: 1(vi) What does it show when a chemical reaction is exothermic?

(a) It shows the bonds which break are weaker than those are formed. (b) It shows the bond which break are stronger than those are formed. (c) Exothermic nature of the reaction is not concerned with bond formation or bond breakage. (d) It shows that the reactants are more stable than the products.
Correct answer: It shows the bonds which break are weaker than those are formed.

Q: 1(vii) When NaOH and HCl are mixed the temperature increases. The reaction is:

(a) endothermic with a positive enthalpy change. (b) endothermic with a negative enthalpy change. (c) exothermic with a positive enthalpy change. (d) exothermic with a negative enthalpy change.
Correct answer: exothermic with a negative enthalpy change.

Q: 1(viii) The average bond dissociation energy for the C-H bond is 412 kJ mol-1. Which of the following process will have enthalpy change close to 412 kJ mol-1?

(a) CH4(g) -> C(g) + 2H2(g) (b) CH4(g) -> C(g) + 2H2(g) (as printed, same as (a)) (c) CH4(g) -> C(g) + 4H(g) (d) CH4(g) -> CH3(g) + H(g)
Correct answer: CH4(g) -> CH3(g) + H(g)

Q: 1(ix) The average bond energies for O - O and O = O are 146 and 496 kJ mol-1 respectively. Find the enthalpy in kJ for the following reaction? H-O-O-H(g) -> H-O-H(g) + 1/2 O=O(g)

(a) -102kJ (b) +102kJ (c) +350kJ (d) +394kJ
Correct answer: -102kJ

Q: 1(x) Why does the following exothermic reaction not occur? C(Diamond) -> C(Graphite), delta H = -3 kJ mol-1

(a) Structure of diamond is more stable than that of graphite. (b) Diamond has strong covalent bonds than does the graphite. (c) The change from diamond to graphite has high activation energy. (d) Density of graphite is less then that of diamond.
Correct answer: The change from diamond to graphite has high activation energy.

mcqs.q: 1(i) The following reaction is an exothermic reaction. H2 + Cl2 --(Sunlight)--> 2HCl. From where does the energy come to break the bonds of H2 and Cl2?
options: By collisions of the molecules with the walls of the container
mcqs.why: This reaction between hydrogen and chlorine is set off by sunlight: it is the light energy that supplies the energy needed to break the H-H and Cl-Cl bonds and start the reaction. That is why the mixture can stay unreacted in the dark and reacts in sunlight.

mcqs.q: 1(ii) Which of the following reactions has the least value of activation energy?
mcqs.why: The precipitation reaction between NaCl(aq) and AgNO3(aq) takes place between ions already free in solution, so it happens almost instantly on mixing - it has the least activation energy. The other reactions involve breaking covalent bonds in molecules, which needs much more activation energy.

mcqs.q: 1(iii) Formation of which hydrogen halide from the elements is an endothermic reaction?
mcqs.why: The formation of HF, HCl and HBr from their elements gives out heat (exothermic), but the formation of hydrogen iodide, HI, from H2 and I2 absorbs heat - it is the endothermic one among the hydrogen halides.

mcqs.q: 1(iv) What are the products of anaerobic respiration?
mcqs.why: Anaerobic respiration breaks down glucose without using oxygen. In yeast it produces ethanol, and the energy released is stored as ATP (the book's keyed answer includes the water of the aqueous medium). Aerobic respiration, by contrast, gives CO2 + H2O with much more ATP.

mcqs.q: 1(v) Which reaction do you expect to be a reversible reaction? (Energy profiles (a)-(d) are shown in the book.)
options: profile (a): products C + D far below reactants A + B (strongly exothermic)
profile (b): products C + D at almost the same energy as reactants A + B
profile (c): products C + D moderately above reactants A + B
profile (d): products C + D far above reactants A + B (strongly endothermic)
mcqs.why: A reaction is reversible when the products can change back into reactants at a comparable rate. That happens when reactants and products have almost the same energy, as in profile (b), so the enthalpy change is small in both directions; in strongly exothermic (a) or strongly endothermic (d) profiles the reverse reaction is negligible.

mcqs.q: 1(vi) What does it show when a chemical reaction is exothermic?
options: It shows the bonds which break are weaker than those are formed.
It shows the bond which break are stronger than those are formed.
Exothermic nature of the reaction is not concerned with bond formation or bond breakage.
It shows that the reactants are more stable than the products.
mcqs.why: In every reaction, energy is absorbed to break the bonds of reactants and released when new bonds form in the products. If the reaction is exothermic, more energy is released in forming the product bonds than was absorbed in breaking the reactant bonds - i.e. the bonds broken are weaker than the bonds formed.

mcqs.q: 1(vii) When NaOH and HCl are mixed the temperature increases. The reaction is:
options: endothermic with a positive enthalpy change.
endothermic with a negative enthalpy change.
exothermic with a positive enthalpy change.
exothermic with a negative enthalpy change.
mcqs.why: When NaOH and HCl are mixed, the temperature of the mixture rises, so heat is evolved: the neutralisation is exothermic. For an exothermic reaction the products have less enthalpy than the reactants, so the enthalpy change is negative.

mcqs.q: 1(viii) The average bond dissociation energy for the C-H bond is 412 kJ mol-1. Which of the following process will have enthalpy change close to 412 kJ mol-1?
mcqs.why: The average C-H bond energy (412 kJ mol-1) is the energy needed to break ONE C-H bond in one mole. CH4(g) -> CH3(g) + H(g) breaks exactly one C-H bond, so its enthalpy change is close to 412 kJ mol-1. CH4(g) -> C(g) + 4H(g) breaks all four C-H bonds and needs about 4 x 412 kJ mol-1.

mcqs.q: 1(ix) The average bond energies for O - O and O = O are 146 and 496 kJ mol-1 respectively. Find the enthalpy in kJ for the following reaction? H-O-O-H(g) -> H-O-H(g) + 1/2 O=O(g)
mcqs.why: Working: in H-O-O-H -> H-O-H + 1/2 O=O, the two O-H bonds are present on both sides and cancel. Bonds broken: one O-O bond = 146 kJ. Bonds formed: 1/2 O=O bond = 1/2 x 496 = 248 kJ. Enthalpy change = energy absorbed - energy released = 146 - 248 = -102 kJ. The negative sign shows the reaction is exothermic.

mcqs.q: 1(x) Why does the following exothermic reaction not occur? C(Diamond) -> C(Graphite), delta H = -3 kJ mol-1
options: Structure of diamond is more stable than that of graphite.
Diamond has strong covalent bonds than does the graphite.
The change from diamond to graphite has high activation energy.
Density of graphite is less then that of diamond.
mcqs.why: The change C(diamond) -> C(graphite) has delta H = -3 kJ mol-1, so it is thermodynamically favourable, yet it does not occur because the rearrangement of the diamond structure has a very high activation energy. Diamond is therefore metastable - it survives indefinitely at ordinary temperatures.

lessons.title: Questions for Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 2(i) What is the difference between enthalpy and enthalpy change?

Enthalpy (H) is the total heat content (internal energy) stored in a substance or system. Enthalpy change (delta H) is the amount of heat absorbed or evolved during a change or reaction at constant pressure; it is the difference between the enthalpy of the products and the enthalpy of the reactants, delta H = H(products) - H(reactants).

Q: 2(ii) Why is breaking of a bond an endothermic process?

A bond holds atoms together because the bonded atoms are at a lower energy than the separated atoms. To break a bond, energy equal to the bond energy must be supplied from outside to pull the atoms apart against their attraction. Since heat energy is absorbed from the surroundings, bond breaking is always an endothermic process.

Q: 2(iii) Depict the transition state for the following reaction. H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl

Transition state for H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl (describe and draw in the notes): at the top of the energy barrier the H-H and Cl-Cl bonds are partly broken and the H-Cl bonds are partly formed; the activated complex can be written as [H...H...Cl...Cl] with dotted (partial) bonds, in which all four atoms are loosely joined together. It exists for an instant only, then falls apart either into 2HCl (successful collision) or back into H2 + Cl2.

Q: 2(iv) Draw the reaction profiles for two exothermic reactions one of which moves faster than the other.

Draw two exothermic reaction profiles (energy against path of reaction) with products below reactants in both. The faster reaction has the lower activation energy (a smaller hump between reactants and the peak), so its curve rises to a lower peak; the slower reaction has a higher peak (larger activation energy). The enthalpy change (drop from reactants to products) may be similar in both; it is the height of the barrier, not the drop, that decides the speed.

Q: 2(v) What is the role of glycogen in our body?

Glycogen is the storage carbohydrate of our body, stored mainly in the liver and muscles. It acts as an energy reserve: when the blood glucose level falls, glycogen is broken down into glucose to supply energy; when glucose is in excess, it is converted into glycogen and stored. It is the animal equivalent of starch in plants.

mcqs.q: Enthalpy (H) of a substance or system is:
options: The heat it gives out in every reaction
Its total heat content (internal energy) stored in it
The energy of its electrons only
mcqs.why: Enthalpy (H) is the total heat content (internal energy) stored in a substance or system. The enthalpy change, delta H, is the heat absorbed or evolved during a change at constant pressure.

mcqs.q: The enthalpy change of a reaction is defined as:
mcqs.why: Enthalpy change is the difference between the enthalpy of the products and the enthalpy of the reactants: delta H = H(products) - H(reactants). It is negative for exothermic reactions (products lower in enthalpy) and positive for endothermic ones.

mcqs.q: Breaking a chemical bond is always an endothermic process because:
options: Energy must be supplied from outside to pull the bonded atoms apart against their attraction
Bonds release energy when they break
Atoms have no attraction for each other
Heat is produced whenever atoms separate
mcqs.why: Bonded atoms are at a lower energy than separated atoms. To break a bond, energy equal to the bond energy must be supplied to pull the atoms apart against their attraction, so heat is absorbed from the surroundings - bond breaking is always endothermic.

mcqs.q: The transition state of a reaction is:
options: The final state of the products
The unstable, highest-energy arrangement in which old bonds are partly broken and new bonds are partly formed
The starting state of the reactants
A stable intermediate that can be isolated
mcqs.why: At the top of the energy barrier the reacting atoms form an activated complex - the transition state - in which the old bonds are partly broken and the new bonds are partly formed. It exists for an instant only, then falls apart into products or back into reactants.

mcqs.q: For the reaction H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl, the transition state can be represented as:
options: [H...H...Cl...Cl] with dotted (partial) bonds joining all four atoms loosely
mcqs.why: At the transition state of H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl, the H-H and Cl-Cl bonds are partly broken and the H-Cl bonds are partly formed; the activated complex is written [H...H...Cl...Cl] with dotted partial bonds. It then falls apart into 2HCl (successful collision) or back into H2 + Cl2.

mcqs.q: Of two exothermic reactions, the faster one has:
options: Products with higher energy than reactants
The lower activation energy (a smaller energy hump)
mcqs.why: On a reaction profile, both exothermic reactions end below their reactants, but the faster reaction has the lower peak - the smaller activation energy. The speed is decided by the height of the barrier, not by the enthalpy drop, which may be similar in both.

mcqs.q: The rate of a reaction is decided by:
options: The height of the activation-energy barrier, not by the enthalpy change
The mass of the reactants only
mcqs.why: A reaction with a large enthalpy drop can still be very slow if its activation energy is high (e.g. diamond changing to graphite). It is the height of the energy barrier between reactants and the transition state that decides how fast the reaction goes.

mcqs.q: Glycogen is stored mainly in the:
mcqs.why: Glycogen is the storage carbohydrate of the body, stored mainly in the liver and muscles. It is the animal equivalent of starch in plants.

mcqs.q: The role of glycogen in the body is to:
options: Act as an energy reserve that is broken down to glucose when blood glucose falls
mcqs.why: When the blood glucose level falls, glycogen is broken down into glucose to supply energy; when glucose is in excess, it is converted into glycogen and stored. Glycogen is therefore the body's energy reserve.

mcqs.q: When blood glucose is in excess, the body:
options: Converts it into protein at once
Converts it into glycogen and stores it
mcqs.why: Excess glucose is converted into glycogen and stored in the liver and muscles. The stored glycogen is changed back into glucose whenever the blood glucose level falls and energy is needed.

lessons.title: Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 3(i) Physical changes which usually occur around us are given in the table. Write down whether they are exothermic or endothermic. (Conversion of hydrated salt into anhydrous salt; Burning of paper; Vapourizing liquid nitrogen; Evaporation of dry ice; Conduction of electricity by metals; Dissolving ammonium chloride in water; Formation of rain from clouds; Dissolving sodium carbonate in water.)

Conversion of hydrated salt into anhydrous salt: Endothermic (heat must be supplied to drive off the water of crystallisation). Burning of paper: Exothermic (heat is given out; strictly it is a chemical change listed in the table). Vapourizing liquid nitrogen: Endothermic (it absorbs heat from the surroundings to boil). Evaporation of dry ice: Endothermic (sublimation absorbs heat). Conduction of electricity by metals: neither a state change nor a reaction; in itself it involves no enthalpy change (a conductor warms only slightly because of resistance). Dissolving ammonium chloride in water: Endothermic (the solution becomes cold). Formation of rain from clouds: Exothermic (condensation of water vapour releases heat). Dissolving sodium carbonate in water: Exothermic (the solution becomes warm).

Q: 3(ii) Explain why the reaction between atmospheric gases oxygen and nitrogen does not take place under normal conditions? But in the presence of lightning these gases react to give NO. The reaction stops as soon as the lightning stops.

Nitrogen and oxygen molecules are very stable: the N triple bond is extremely strong, so the activation energy of the reaction N2 + O2 -> 2NO is very high, and at normal temperatures practically no collisions are energetic enough to start it. Lightning provides an enormous amount of energy (temperatures of thousands of degrees), so the molecules gain enough energy to react and form NO. When the lightning stops, the temperature falls, the supply of activation energy ends, and the reaction stops.

Q: 3(iii) A reaction between natural gas (CH4) and atmospheric oxygen does not take place when you mix them. As soon as you show a burning match stick, the reaction starts immediately and then it continues until one or both of the reactants is/are used up. Explain.

Methane and oxygen at room temperature do not react because their molecules do not have the activation energy needed to break the bonds and start the reaction. A burning match supplies this activation energy to a small portion of the mixture, which starts burning. The reaction is strongly exothermic, and the heat released provides the activation energy for the neighbouring molecules, so the reaction becomes self-sustaining and continues until one or both reactants are used up.

mcqs.q: Converting a hydrated salt into its anhydrous salt is:
options: Exothermic, because the salt becomes lighter
Endothermic, because heat must be supplied to drive off the water of crystallisation
mcqs.why: To remove the water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt, heat must be supplied continuously. Since heat is absorbed from the surroundings, the change is endothermic.

mcqs.q: Burning of paper is:
options: A physical change with no heat effect
mcqs.why: Burning of paper gives out heat and light to the surroundings, so it is exothermic. (It is strictly a chemical change, although it was listed in the book's table of changes.)

mcqs.q: Vaporising liquid nitrogen is an endothermic change because it:
options: Absorbs heat from the surroundings in order to boil
mcqs.why: Liquid nitrogen boils at a very low temperature by taking heat from its surroundings - that is why it feels intensely cold and is used as a coolant. Absorbing heat makes vaporisation an endothermic change.

mcqs.q: Evaporation of dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) is:
options: Exothermic, because a gas is produced
Neither, because dry ice is already cold
mcqs.why: Dry ice sublimes - it changes directly from solid to gas - and sublimation absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the evaporation of dry ice is an endothermic physical change.

mcqs.q: Dissolving ammonium chloride in water is endothermic because:
mcqs.why: When ammonium chloride dissolves, it absorbs heat from the water, so the temperature of the solution falls and the beaker feels cold - the sign of an endothermic process.

mcqs.q: Formation of rain from clouds is an exothermic change because:
options: Condensation of water vapour releases heat
Water vapour absorbs heat to condense
Rain falls from a great height
mcqs.why: Rain forms when water vapour in clouds condenses into liquid droplets. Condensation is the reverse of evaporation: it releases the latent heat that was absorbed during evaporation, so it is exothermic.

mcqs.q: Dissolving sodium carbonate in water is:
options: Endothermic, because the solution becomes cold
Exothermic, because the solution becomes warm
Neither, because dissolving is not a change
mcqs.why: When sodium carbonate dissolves in water, heat is given out and the solution becomes warm - unlike ammonium chloride, whose dissolving makes the solution cold. Dissolving sodium carbonate is therefore exothermic.

mcqs.q: Conduction of electricity by metals, in itself:
options: Involves no enthalpy change (it is neither a state change nor a reaction)
mcqs.why: Passing electricity through a metal is not a change of state or a chemical reaction, so in itself it has no enthalpy change; a conductor warms only slightly because of electrical resistance.

mcqs.q: Oxygen and nitrogen of the air do not react under normal conditions because:
options: Nitrogen is an inert gas in all conditions
The N2 molecule has an extremely strong triple bond, so the activation energy is very high
mcqs.why: The reaction N2 + O2 -> 2NO needs the very strong N triple bond to be broken, so its activation energy is extremely high. At normal temperatures practically no collisions are energetic enough to start the reaction.

mcqs.q: During lightning, nitrogen and oxygen react to form NO, but the reaction stops as soon as the lightning stops because:
options: The temperature falls and the supply of activation energy ends
All the nitrogen is used up in one flash
Rain washes the NO away instantly
mcqs.why: Lightning provides enormous energy (temperatures of thousands of degrees), so N2 and O2 molecules gain enough energy to react. When the lightning stops, the temperature falls, no more molecules have the activation energy, and the reaction stops.

lessons.title: Descriptive Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 4(i) Find out the enthalpy change of the following reaction using the given data. N2 + O2 -> 2NO. Bond dissociation energy of N2 = 958.38 kJ/mol; Bond dissociation energy of O2 = 498 kJ/mol; Bond formation energy of NO = -626 kJ/mol.

Given data: N2 + O2 -> 2NO; bond dissociation energy of N2 = 958.38 kJ/mol; bond dissociation energy of O2 = 498 kJ/mol; bond formation energy of NO = -626 kJ/mol. Step 1 - Formula: enthalpy change = energy absorbed in breaking bonds + energy released in forming bonds. Step 2 - Energy absorbed in breaking 1 mol of N triple bonds and 1 mol of O double bonds = 958.38 + 498 = 1456.38 kJ. Step 3 - Energy released in forming 2 mol of NO bonds = 2 x (-626) = -1252 kJ. Step 4 - Add: delta H = 1456.38 - 1252 = +204.38 kJ/mol. Final answer: the enthalpy change is +204.38 kJ/mol; the positive sign shows the reaction is endothermic.

Q: 4(ii) Explain the difference between the terms heat and enthalpy.

Heat is energy in transit: it is the energy transferred between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference, and it exists only while the transfer is taking place. Enthalpy is a property of the system itself: the total heat content stored in the substances of the system. We cannot measure the absolute enthalpy, but we can measure the heat exchanged, which at constant pressure equals the enthalpy change of the process.

Q: 4(iii) Explain why formation of a bond is always an exothermic process.

Atoms attract one another through the bond, and the bonded state is more stable and of lower energy than the separated atoms. When free atoms come together to form a bond, they fall to this lower energy state, and the excess energy is released as heat. Hence bond formation always gives out energy and is an exothermic process, the reverse of bond breaking.

Q: 4(iv) Explain the role of lipids in our body.

Lipids (fats and oils) are the concentrated energy store of the body: gram for gram they provide more than twice the energy of carbohydrates. They also form the membranes of cells, act as an insulating layer under the skin that keeps the body warm, protect delicate organs as a cushion, and carry the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K into the body.

Q: 4(v) Explain the following terms. Activation energy, Transition state, Aerobic respiration

Activation energy: the minimum extra energy which the reacting molecules must possess (over and above their average energy) so that their collisions result in a reaction; it is the height of the energy barrier between reactants and products. Transition state: the unstable, highest-energy arrangement of atoms formed momentarily at the top of the barrier, in which old bonds are partly broken and new bonds are partly formed; it immediately falls apart into products or back into reactants. Aerobic respiration: the breakdown of glucose in the cells in the presence of oxygen, C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy (ATP); it releases much more energy than anaerobic respiration.

mcqs.q: Using bond energies (N2 = 958.38, O2 = 498, NO formation = -626 kJ/mol), the enthalpy change of N2 + O2 -> 2NO is:
mcqs.why: Working: energy absorbed in breaking bonds = 958.38 + 498 = 1456.38 kJ. Energy released in forming 2 mol of NO bonds = 2 x (-626) = -1252 kJ. delta H = 1456.38 - 1252 = +204.38 kJ/mol.

mcqs.q: The reaction N2 + O2 -> 2NO, with delta H = +204.38 kJ/mol, is:
mcqs.why: The enthalpy change is positive (+204.38 kJ/mol), meaning heat is absorbed from the surroundings: the reaction is endothermic. This agrees with the fact that it needs lightning or very high temperatures to take place.

mcqs.q: Heat differs from enthalpy in that heat is:
options: A property stored permanently in a substance
Energy in transit between a system and its surroundings due to a temperature difference
mcqs.why: Heat is energy in transit: it is transferred between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference and exists only while the transfer is taking place. Enthalpy, by contrast, is a property of the system itself - its total stored heat content.

mcqs.q: We cannot measure the absolute enthalpy of a system, but the heat exchanged at constant pressure equals:
options: The enthalpy change of the process
mcqs.why: Absolute enthalpy cannot be measured, but the heat absorbed or evolved in a process at constant pressure is exactly its enthalpy change, delta H - which is what calorimetry measures.

mcqs.q: Formation of a bond is always an exothermic process because:
options: The bonded atoms are in a lower, more stable energy state, and the excess energy is released as heat
Atoms gain energy when they join together
Bonds form only at high temperatures
Free atoms have less energy than bonded atoms
mcqs.why: Atoms attract one another through the bond, and the bonded state is more stable and of lower energy than the separated atoms. When free atoms join, they fall to this lower energy state and the excess energy is released as heat - bond formation is always exothermic, the reverse of bond breaking.

mcqs.q: Lipids (fats and oils) are the body's concentrated energy store because, gram for gram, they provide:
options: Exactly the same energy as carbohydrates
More than twice the energy of carbohydrates
mcqs.why: Lipids are the concentrated energy store of the body: gram for gram they provide more than twice the energy obtained from carbohydrates, which is why excess food energy is stored as fat.

mcqs.q: Besides storing energy, lipids in the body also:
options: Form cell membranes, insulate the body and carry fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K
mcqs.why: Lipids form the membranes of cells, act as an insulating layer under the skin that keeps the body warm, cushion and protect delicate organs, and carry the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K into the body.

mcqs.q: Activation energy is:
options: The total energy of the products
The heat released by every reaction
The energy of the transition state minus the energy of the products only
The minimum extra energy reacting molecules must possess so that their collisions result in a reaction
mcqs.why: Activation energy is the height of the energy barrier between reactants and products: the minimum extra energy, over and above their average energy, which reacting molecules must possess so that their collisions actually result in a reaction.

mcqs.q: The transition state of a reaction:
options: Exists for an instant only, then falls apart into products or back into reactants
Can be collected in a bottle
Is the most stable state of the system
mcqs.why: The transition state is the unstable, highest-energy arrangement of atoms at the top of the barrier, with old bonds partly broken and new bonds partly formed. It cannot be isolated: it immediately falls apart either into products or back into reactants.

mcqs.q: Aerobic respiration differs from anaerobic respiration in that it:
options: Breaks down glucose in the presence of oxygen and releases much more energy
Produces ethanol as the main product
mcqs.why: Aerobic respiration: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy (ATP). Because the glucose is completely broken down using oxygen, it releases much more energy than anaerobic respiration, which works without oxygen.

lessons.title: Investigative Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 5(i) Why is it essential to cook some of the food items while others we can eat without cooking?

Cooking applies heat, which breaks down tough fibres and complex molecules (such as starch and proteins), kills harmful germs, and makes the food soft, digestible and safe; raw meat, pulses and many vegetables therefore need cooking. Foods such as fruits, salads and milk products are already soft, easily digested and safe, and cooking would destroy some of their vitamins, so they can be eaten without cooking.

Q: 5(ii) Why does fireworks look spectacular? What type of chemical compounds undergo chemical reactions during this activity?

Fireworks contain mixtures of oxidising agents (such as nitrates and chlorates of potassium) with fuels (charcoal, sulphur) and metal salts. On ignition, rapid exothermic combustion reactions release a large amount of energy as heat and light; the vaporised metal salts give the characteristic colours (strontium red, barium green, sodium yellow, copper blue), and the fast production of gases produces the bursts, sparks and bangs. The spectacular effect is the sudden release of chemical energy as light, heat, sound and expanding gases.

mcqs.q: Some foods must be cooked before eating mainly because heat:
options: Breaks down tough fibres and complex molecules and kills harmful germs
Removes all the water from the food
mcqs.why: Cooking applies heat, which breaks down tough fibres and complex molecules such as starch and proteins, kills harmful germs, and makes food soft, digestible and safe. Raw meat, pulses and many vegetables therefore need cooking.

mcqs.q: Foods such as fruits, salads and milk products can be eaten without cooking because:
options: They are already soft, digestible and safe, and cooking would destroy some of their vitamins
mcqs.why: These foods are already soft, easily digested and safe to eat raw. Cooking them would destroy some of their vitamins, so they are eaten without cooking.

mcqs.q: In fireworks, the oxidising agents used are typically:
mcqs.why: Fireworks contain oxidising agents such as nitrates and chlorates of potassium mixed with fuels. The oxidisers supply the oxygen for the rapid combustion that produces the display.

mcqs.q: The fuels commonly used in fireworks are:
mcqs.why: Charcoal and sulphur act as fuels in fireworks. Mixed with oxidising agents (nitrates, chlorates), they undergo rapid exothermic combustion on ignition, releasing energy as heat and light.

mcqs.q: The red colour in fireworks is produced by salts of:
mcqs.why: Vaporised metal salts give fireworks their characteristic colours: strontium gives red, barium green, sodium yellow and copper blue.

mcqs.q: The green colour in fireworks is produced by salts of:
mcqs.why: Barium salts vaporised in the hot flame of a firework emit green light. (Strontium = red, sodium = yellow, copper = blue.)

mcqs.q: The yellow colour in fireworks is produced by salts of:
mcqs.why: Sodium salts give an intense yellow colour to flames, and are used for the yellow effects in fireworks. (Strontium = red, barium = green, copper = blue.)

mcqs.q: The blue colour in fireworks is produced by salts of:
mcqs.why: Copper salts produce the blue colour in fireworks when vaporised in the flame. (Strontium = red, barium = green, sodium = yellow.)

mcqs.q: The chemical reactions inside a firework are:
options: Rapid exothermic combustion reactions releasing energy as heat, light, sound and expanding gases
mcqs.why: On ignition, the fuel-oxidiser mixture undergoes rapid exothermic combustion, releasing a large amount of energy suddenly as heat and light; the fast production of gases produces the bursts, sparks and bangs.

mcqs.q: The bangs and bursts of fireworks are caused by:
options: The melting of the metal salts
The fast production of large volumes of gas
The fall of the rocket under gravity
mcqs.why: The combustion reactions in a firework produce gases very rapidly in a confined space. The sudden expansion of these hot gases produces the bursts, sparks and bangs of the display.

lessons.title: In-text Exercise & Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Q: In-text Exercise: The preparation of ethyl acetate is commercially very important because it is used as a thinner in paint industry. C2H5OH(l) + CH3COOH(l) <==> (dil. H2SO4) CH3COOC2H5(l) + H2O(l). One way to get the better yield of the product ethyl acetate is to remove water from the reaction mixture as soon as it is formed. Suggest a suitable method to withdraw water from the reaction mixture.

Use concentrated sulphuric acid in place of (or in addition to) the dilute acid catalyst. Concentrated H2SO4 is a powerful dehydrating agent: it absorbs the water as soon as it is formed and removes it from the reaction mixture. With water withdrawn, the reverse reaction (hydrolysis of the ester) cannot proceed, so by Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium keeps shifting to the right and the forward reaction continues until nearly all the alcohol and acid are converted into ethyl acetate. (Removing the ester by distillation as it forms helps in the same way.)

Q: 1(i) What will happen if the rates of forward and reverse reactions are very high?

(a) The equilibrium point will reach very soon. (b) The equilibrium point will reach very late. (c) The reaction will not attain the state of dynamic equilibrium. (d) The reaction will be practically irreversible.
Correct answer: The equilibrium point will reach very soon.

Q: 1(ii) Predict which components of the atmosphere react in the presence of lightning.

(a) N2 and H2O (b) O2 and H2O (c) CO2 and O2 (d) N2 and O2
Correct answer: N2 and O2

Q: 1(iii) An inorganic chemist places one mole of PCl5 in a container A and one mole of each Cl2 and PCl3 in container B. Both the containers were sealed and heated to the same temperature to reach the state of equilibrium. Guess about the composition of mixtures in both the containers.

(a) Both the containers will have the same composition of mixtures. (b) Container A will have more concentration of PCl3 than B. (c) Container A will have less concentration of PCl3 than B. (d) Both the containers will have zero concentration of its reactants.
Correct answer: Both the containers will have the same composition of mixtures.

Q: 1(iv) CaO or lime is used extensively in steel, glass and paper industries. It is produced in a reversible reaction by the decomposition of lime (CaCO3). Choose the conditions to produce maximum amount of lime.

(a) Heating at high temperature in a closed vessel (b) Heating at high temperature in an open vessel (c) Cooling it in a closed vessel (d) Cooling it in an open vessel
Correct answer: Heating at high temperature in an open vessel

Q: 1(v) What condition should be met for the reversible reaction to achieve the state of equilibrium?

(a) All the reactants should be converted into the products. (b) 50% of the reactants should be converted into products. (c) The concentrations of all the reactants and the products should become constant. (d) One of the products should be removed from the reaction mixture.
Correct answer: The concentrations of all the reactants and the products should become constant.

Q: 1(vi) Why the gas starts coming out when you open a can of fizzy drink?

(a) Because the solubility of the gas increases (b) Because the gas is insoluble in water (c) Because the gas is dissolved under pressure hence it comes out when pressure is decreased (d) Because the solubility of the gas decreases at high pressure
Correct answer: Because the gas is dissolved under pressure hence it comes out when pressure is decreased
